**Finding submitted — deviation (fallback cure).**

- **Responsive clause:** Section 1.4 (p0008–p0009) is the only grant running *to* us — access to and the right to use HDI's hosting system plus HDI's software and Content administration tools. Section 6.1's licence (p0038–p0039) runs *from* us to HDI (our Marks) and is not responsive to this rule; Section 10.3's successors-and-assigns provision (p0063) is a general binding clause, not a clear licence-transfer right.
- **Why it fails fallback:** no coverage of our affiliates (even on written notice) and no express transferability of the use rights to a successor in an M&A transaction. The grant is not expressly revocable at will, so this is not walk-away territory.
- **Cure:** one inserted sentence after p0009 extending the Section 1.4 rights to our affiliates on written notice and permitting transfer to an M&A successor — nothing else in Section 1.4 was altered, and no preferred-level extras (perpetuity, irrevocability, contractors) were volunteered.
